title: A plugin's dependency hoists dsh-tools@0.2.0-rc.2 into the profile, so the in-box `tools` row is disabled and the host cannot boot

reported.symptom: after `dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-livedocs` the window flashes and exits; `1 required plugin did not activate`, `agent-loop (required) → tools missing`; then DSH resets the profile (bundles → base+web-app, cordis.patch.yml → []) and every third-party plugin disappears
reported.runtime_trace: dsh: disabling profile plugin row "tools": Plugin @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools@0.2.0-rc.2 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.1-rc.2: requirements {"@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent":"0.2.0-rc.2", ...}
user_hypotheses: the runtime package is simply missing (it is not: it is shadowed by the profile copy)
reinstalling the plugin fixes it (it does not: the hoisted copy comes back)
reported.root_cause: dsh-livedocs declares @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools in dependencies (not peerDependencies), so pnpm materialises 0.2.0-rc.2 at <profile>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools; the resolved row module then fails the version rule against the 0.2.1-rc.2 runtime
reported.fix_verified_by_reporter: not stated by the reporter; the thread documents the boot-failure → profile-reset chain

deviations: the `tools` row belongs to the in-box `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` bundle, not to the profile patch; it is re-mounted in the profile patch layer so the case stays a one-row reconstruction (profile rows and bundle rows resolve through the same resolver, so the attribution is unchanged)
bundles omitted: dsh-base / dsh-web-app are left out to keep the composition minimal

the hoisting plugin's own version (`dsh-livedocs`) is not stated in the report, so its manifest is not reproduced; only the copy it produces (dsh-tools@0.2.0-rc.2, the module the row actually resolves to) is materialised
the report was written before dsh-tools@0.2.1-rc.x was published; the input is the 0.2.0-rc.2 manifest the message names, not today's newest
the profile reset (bundles → 2, cordis.patch.yml → []) is a separate defect and is not modelled
